name: Erastus (the city treasurer)
title: Corinth's financial administrator
summary: Erastus was the city treasurer (oikonomos) in Corinth and one of Paul's coworkers. He was among the few wealthy and high-ranking officials who converted to Christianity in the early church, representing the gospel's breakthrough into the upper levels of society.

keyEvents.title: Greeting from Corinth
keyEvents.description: Paul sends greetings from Erastus, the city treasurer, to the church in Rome, showing his prominent position in both the city and the church.

keyEvents.title: Sent to Macedonia
keyEvents.description: Paul sent Erastus along with Timothy to Macedonia to serve the churches there, while Paul himself remained in Asia.

keyEvents.title: Remained in Corinth
keyEvents.description: In one of his final letters, Paul mentions that Erastus stayed behind in Corinth, which may indicate that he continued his office and service there.
